item.title: Xbox Giving Away 25 Free Games to Some Gamers
item.description:
Xbox is giving away 25 games for completely free to some gamers in the US, but there's a bit of a catch. However, for those who qualify for the Xbox offer, it's a great opportunity to get some popular titles that are free to keep.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Xbox Game Pass is a popular option for gamers, since it offers fans a huge library of games to enjoy for a simple monthly fee. However, for those who aren't interested in subscription services or are just looking to increase the number of permanent games in their libraries, this new offer is a great opportunity.

Skyrim: Best Mods To Use On Xbox

Skyrim mods aren't only on PC, and Xbox players who love Bethesda's open-world RPG should take advantage of the scene available to them.

By Hamza Haq

Xbox Gives Away 25 Games for Free, With a Catch

Xbox is giving away 25 free games to anyone who purchases a Windows 11 PC or Windows 11-based gaming system like the Xbox ROG Ally X20. The list includes some major hits, like The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim , Minecraft Dungeons , and Gears of War: Reloaded . The offer was set to begin on November 2 and run through the end of the year, or until supplies run out, but it seems that it's gone live early, as some players are reporting they've received the offer on their computers or handhelds. Players who want to see if they've already received it should check the Microsoft Store app on their eligible device. However, if it's not there, they should check back after November 2 to see if that's changed.

Free Games Included in Offer

  • Age of Empires 2: Definitive Edition
  • Age of Empires 3: Definitive Edition
  • Age of Mythology: Retold
  • As Dusk Falls
  • Battletoads
  • Blinx: The Time Sweeper
  • Call of Duty WWII
  • Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge
  • DOOM + DOOM 2
  • Fallout 76
  • Fuzion Frenzy
  • Gears of War: Reloaded
  • Gears Tactics
  • Halo: The Master Chief Collection
  • Minecraft Dungeons
  • Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire
  • Quake
  • Quake 2
  • Rise of Nations: Extended Edition
  • The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion
  • The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim
  • The Elder Scrolls Online
  • The Outer Worlds
  • Wolfenstein: The New Order
  • Zoo Tycoon: Ultimate Animal Collection

This offer is a nice bonus for anyone who's been thinking about buying a new PC or a handheld like the ROG Xbox Ally X20. Once players claim the offer, the 25 games should be added to their Microsoft accounts. Eligible device owners need to activate their device and claim the deal before February 12, 2027. All the available games can be played on compatible Windows PCs, and some are also playable on Xbox Series X/S systems with XBOX Play Anywhere.

Gaming can quickly become an expensive hobby, especially if a gamer needs a new console or PC in order to get started. Free-to-play games are one way to ease some of the financial pain, though the presence of microtransactions, gacha, and other paid mechanics can potentially lead to spending money or a slog of a grind without tapping one's real wallet. Thankfully, many developers and publishers regularly give away their games for free, which can often be added to a permanent library and kept indefinitely. The Epic Games Store has been particularly regarded for giving away free games on the regular, but even platforms like Steam regularly have free game opportunities for players.

item.title: Steam Officially Confirms 2 New Free-to-Keep Games for October 2026
item.description:
Steam is giving PC gamers another opportunity to expand their libraries without spending any money, with two more free-to-keep games confirmed for October 2026. Valve's digital storefront regularly features promotions and discounts, but Steam's free-to-keep offers are particularly appealing because players can permanently add games to their accounts without purchasing them.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

October has been a particularly interesting month for Steam users looking for new games, especially with Halloween approaching and plenty of horror-themed releases getting attention. However, not every giveaway has to be a major AAA game to be worth checking out. Steam's smaller indie releases often offer some surprisingly good experiences, and many have earned excellent reviews from players over the years. The latest free-to-keep offerings are a good example, with one focusing on psychological horror and the other offering a much more relaxing puzzle experience.

Cozy Steam Game With Witchcraft Fully Launches to 90% Positive Reviews

Spooky season fans have a fresh cozy witchcraft game to dive into on Steam, with the title already earning 90% positive reviews.

By Charming Holiday

Steam Free-to-Keep Promotion List (October 2026)

  • Asleep: Act One Goes Free-to-Keep on Steam Soon
  • Hexologic Goes Free-to-Keep on Steam Soon

Steam has confirmed two last new free-to-keep games for October 2026: Asleep: Act 1 and Hexologic . Unlike Steam's Free Weekend Promotions, these games won't disappear from a player's account once the promotion ends; they can be permanently kept forever. Right now, it's uncertain when these free PC games will go live on the storefront, but fans should check their Steam pages daily until then to be sure to grab them:

Asleep: Act 1 (Joining Steam's Free-to-Keep Promotion Soon)

Asleep: Act 1 is probably the more interesting of the two for horror fans, particularly with Halloween just around the corner. Released in May 2024, the game is a 2D psychological horror adventure game that follows Ana Lúcia, a young woman trapped in a disturbing world where reality and nightmares begin to overlap. Players must explore unsettling environments, solve puzzles, and avoid dangerous creatures, with light playing an important role in survival. Different enemies react to light in different ways, meaning players need to think carefully about how they approach each encounter. Asleep: Act 1 has also earned Very Positive reviews on Steam, with 92% of its user reviews being favorable.

Hexologic (Joining Steam's Free-to-Keep Promotion Soon)

Meanwhile, Hexologic offers a completely different experience, combining elements of Sudoku with colorful hexagonal puzzles to challenge players to place numbers across hexagonal grids while making sure the values add up correctly. The puzzle game concept is relatively simple, but the puzzles become increasingly complex as players progress. Its relaxing soundtrack and colorful presentation also make it a good option for anyone looking for something less intense than Asleep: Act 1 . Interestingly, Hexologic has an Overwhelmingly Positive review rating on Steam, with 96% of its user reviews being positive.

Both Asleep: Act 1 and Hexologic are worth claiming when they become available, even for players who don't intend to start them immediately. The easiest way to claim either title is to visit its Steam store pages (linked above) while the promotion is active and add it to an account. With November approaching, there will undoubtedly be more discounts and promotions to watch for, but these two indie Steam games offer another opportunity to pick up something new without spending a dime.

item.title: 7 NES Masterpieces Every Gamer Should Experience, Ranked
item.description:
The Nintendo Entertainment System 's glory days ended a long time ago, but its legacy is beyond reproach. Despite running on arguably the most important console of all time, NES games tend to be overlooked in favor of SNES, Genesis, and PS1 releases. There is a reason most indie throwbacks target the 16-bit era and not its 8-bit predecessor: that generation gets way more love. Honestly, I get it, as not too many NES games stand the test of time; however, a few releases really should be played by most folks.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Why? Well, these NES games either created or popularized genres, or helped evolve the gaming industry in some form or another. While I would not necessarily say that they have all aged flawlessly, they are all still very playable, and some of them are as brilliant as they were 40 years ago.

7 Contra Is Pure Run-And-Gun Goodness

You Cannot Go Wrong With The Best

A rare example of a NES game surpassing the arcade version, Contra holds up incredibly well, and you could even argue that it perfected the run-and-gun formula right out of the gate. Simple as it might be, the gameplay shines due to its top-notch controls, pacing, and responsiveness, all of which are timeless and will always be easy to appreciate. The 3D tunnel stages were also quite cool for the era, even if they might not be all that impressive nowadays.

More Games

Nowadays, these types of games aren't all that common, and newer releases don't typically offer anything all that much better than the classics. Hell, Konami only seems to remember that Contra exists every 5 years or so, and the quality of the post-2000s releases is all over the place. You cannot go wrong with the original console version, though.

6 Mike Tyson’s Punch-Out!! Still Packs An Incredible Punch

The NES Still Lets You Feel Like A Champ

Mike Tyson’s Punch-Out!! has aged better than nearly any other NES game. Sure, the gameplay loop isn't exactly complex, but it's executed to pretty much perfection. While presented as a sports title, Punch-Out is really a rhythm game where you have to read your opponent's movements and then execute a counter. Each new fighter introduces new routines and moves, and the challenge level increases very quickly.

More than anything, Punch-Out is still wildly unique. Nintendo almost never revisits the franchise, and these types of fights/rhythm games/whatever aren't a thing in modern gaming. Even decades later, Punch-Out still feels one-of-a-kind, both as a game and a series.

5 Classic NES Games That Hold Up As 10/10 Masterpieces

Most NES games are easy to appreciate but hard to love, but these masterpeices have stood the test of time so well that they still feel perfect.

13
By Mark Sammut

5 Vice: Project Doom Is An Underrated NES Masterpiece

The Console Has More Than Just Mario, Zelda, And Mega Man

For the most part, I am focusing on landmark NES games that are just synonymous with the generation, but I wanted to include one title that didn't garner that level of exposure. Project: Vice Doom came out late in the console's lifespan, at a point when interest had already shifted to the Genesis and the SNES; consequently, not all that many people were interested in a release on outdated hardware by a developer with no real name value.

The thing is, Project: Vice Doom sits among the NES' most impressive games, in terms of production value and even ambition. Aicom put together a campaign that cycles through three gameplay styles (shooting, driving, and side-scrolling), all of which play incredibly well and look pretty darn good. The B-movie story screams late '80s and early '90s, and I mean that in the best possible way.

If nothing else, Project: Vice Doom serves as a prime example that the NES had way more quality than just games that launched franchises.

4 The Legend Of Zelda Deserves Endless Respect And Love

Even If It Hasn't Aged Perfectly

In the intro, I went on a whole spiel about some of these releases not necessarily aging flawlessly, and The Legend of Zelda is the game I was thinking about. Don't get me wrong, Nintendo put together something truly special in 1986, delivering a level of freedom that was absolutely unheard of at the time.

LoZ 's puzzles and dungeons are still easy enough to appreciate nowadays, although you need to sit through quite a few growing pains to really enjoy the overall experience. Still, LoZ is such a historically significant game that everybody should give it a try, just to see first-hand what Nintendo accomplished and how far gaming has come.

4 Forgotten NES Games Better Than The Legend Of Zelda

The Legend of Zelda might be one of the NES's most important games, but these forgotten NES gems are more fun to play today.

By Mark Sammut

3 Mega Man 2 Is The Start Of One Heck Of A Hot Streak

The Blue Bomber's Explosion

There are way too many Mega Man games on the NES, and they are all quite brilliant, except for the first entry. Although arguments could be made for all of its immediate sequels, Mega Man 2 is generally regarded as the franchise's peak, especially since it laid the foundation for everything else that followed. It also saved the Blue Bomber after the first game failed to really hit the mark.

Capcom refuses to stop re-releasing these early Mega Man games, and for good reason: they are still as awesome as ever. Mega Man 2 is hard-as-hell but also mostly fair, and the non-linear boss design lets players map their route, even if certain orders are more logical than others.

Start with Mega Man 2 and just progress through the franchise's NES games until you feel burned out. That's what I did.

2 Kirby’s Adventure Is The Final NES Masterpiece

You Cannot Go Wrong With The Inhaler

Well, we cannot exactly ignore the NES's swan song, can we? Kirby’s Adventure was released in 1993, when the console was basically already a relic. Nintendo and HAL Laboratory had no need to go all out on the NES by this point, but that's exactly what they did with this colorful and experimental masterpiece.

Introducing the adorable Lovecraftian monster's copy-ability system, which is still a fixture all these decades later, Kirby's Adventure lets you take up more than 20 transformations. Combined with parallax scrolling, minigames, and a visual style that absolutely pops from the screen, this classic barely looks like a NES game. Very few 8-bit games rival their 16-bit counterparts in their presentation, but Kirby's Adventure certainly achieves that.

1 Super Mario Bros. 3 Is What It Is

The Ultimate NES Game

It's Super Mario Bros. 3 ; nobody needs to be told that they should play it. It's ​​​​​​​Super Mario Bros. 3 , the absolute peak of 8-bit platformers. Some might argue it is the greatest 2D Mario game, although Super Mario World certainly has something to say about that. The first Mario game is a must-play as well, but not quite to the same extent as the third.

item.title: New Switch 2 JRPG Like Chrono Trigger Takes Square Enix's HD-2D Formula to Another Dimension
item.description:
There were many great-looking games at the recent Nintendo Indie World showcase, but one that stood out to me was Threads of Time . A time-traveling JRPG with eye-catching HD-2D graphics, Threads of Time is both a throwback to classic genre aesthetics and an embrace of retro-style graphics that are becoming more prominent in new games. The most popular users of HD-2D graphics right now is Square Enix, and while it's great that the developer is leading the charge, Threads of Time raises the bar in terms of overall visual style.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Square Enix has released some great HD-2D JRPGs over the past few years. Games like Octopath Traveler and its sequels kickstarted the industry trend, and it has been a wonderful fit for new JRPGs. HD-2D graphics pay homage to the 90s and early 2000s-era JRPGs while also innovating the genre. Seeing a game like Threads of Time that is so clearly inspired by Square Enix's HD-2D formula proves that the trend is catching on, but it also showcases just how much further Square Enix could push these graphics in its own games.

item.title: Cult of the Lamb Just Fixed One of Steam's Most Annoying Achievement Problems
item.description:
Unlocking achievements is just as important as completing a game, and this is true for many PC players. And to be quite honest, this is true not only when it comes to video games. There is just something about seeing that 100% completion status, especially after spending hundreds of hours working towards the goal. Unfortunately, Steam has one very annoying problem with achievements. To be more specific, the release of new DLCs, like Cult of the Lamb 's Woolhaven, could sometimes interfere with players' ability to maintain their completion status, even if everything in the base game has already been unlocked.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Thankfully, Valve introduced the Steam Achievement Sets in beta on October 15, 2026, which basically allowed developers to start addressing this issue. Then, later on October 19, 2026, it was confirmed that Cult of the Lamb had separated the achievements belonging to its Woolhaven expansion from those of the base game. Many players would agree that this is a welcome change, especially considering that this way developers should be able to introduce more content without taking anything away from the players. However, what's more important is that this highlights why completing games shouldn't require purchasing every single expansion that comes out, even years after the original release.

Steam Officially Makes Open-World Game 100% Free, Plus an Additional Freebie

Two new Steam promotions let users pick up a free open-world survival crafting game and spend time in another game for free.

By Joshua Duckworth

Completing a Game Shouldn't Require Buying Every DLC

The previous achievement system had a lot of issues, with one of them being that players could lose access to 100% completion only because a new expansion became available. Imagine a player's surprise when they have unlocked every achievement in the base game, only to discover that additional objectives have appeared and completing them requires purchasing a separate DLC. Sure, some people feel more inclined to purchase the expansion when this happens, but others find it extremely frustrating and may sometimes even refuse to buy it just because they feel forced.

Of course, Steam's new DLC Sets offer a much more reasonable approach, with the system only counting DLC achievements towards completion for the people who actually own the corresponding content. In other words, it's simply not necessary to finish the DLC content to complete the base game. To be quite honest, being expected to complete something that you simply do not own in order to achieve 100% completion is just unfair, so this new approach will most probably be appreciated by a lot of people.

Achievement Sets Make Tracking Progress Much Easier

Another issue with the previous approach that is worth mentioning is that new achievements could very easily interfere with accomplishments that players had spent years earning. And this is particularly important for games that keep receiving updates even years after their initial release. This can be especially frustrating for veterans who pride themselves on having achieved 100% completion. However, Steam's Achievement Sets take care of all the details because, according to Valve's official documentation, developers can organize achievements around different game modes, chapters, and other categories, which gives the studios a lot of flexibility when designing their achievement systems, especially for those who offer different types of content.

It's important to mention that Achievement Sets are still in beta, so whether other developers will adopt the feature remains to be seen.

Moreover, the previous system meant that having achievements from the base game and multiple expansions in the same list could make it very difficult to figure out which objectives belonged where. And although this is not always a problem, it is very annoying when we're talking about games with huge achievement lists. What's more, the system also supports separate artwork and links to the corresponding DLC's Steam page, so it's easier to identify what each set really represents. And although these may seem like minor improvements, they can make achievement hunting a lot more straightforward. Ultimately, what really matters is that players spend time actually completing objectives rather than sitting there trying to figure out how to deal with this giant mess of achievements.

Cult of the Lamb Sets an Example for Other Steam Developers

Maybe the most important aspect of Cult of the Lamb adopting Achievement Sets is that it really demonstrates how games can benefit from Steam's new feature. According to Valve's official Steamworks documentation, these sets can be configured directly through Steamworks, and developers don't have to make any additional changes to the games' code. This means that old games don't have to develop new achievement systems or wait until their next release to implement this feature. They can simply reorganize their achievements and address some issues that have been ignored for years.

Cult of the Lamb's Best New Switch 2 Upgrade Has Nothing to Do with Graphics
Cult of the Lamb's New Halloween Event Proves Old Rewards Still Matter
New Switch 2 Roguelike Makes Paid Upgrades Harder to Defend

It's important to mention that Achievement Sets are still in beta, so whether other developers will adopt the feature remains to be seen. In any case, Cult of the Lamb is setting a good example by taking advantage of the system, and hopefully more studios will follow it, especially those who are big fans of new expansions. It would also be interesting to see whether we make any further improvements to achievements; after all, this is a new feature, and its long-term usefulness depends on how many people use it and whether their feedback is taken seriously.

8 /10
